question: What is the main goal of organizing a nursing unit?

options.A: Eliminating the need for nursing documentation
options.B: Reducing the overall number of patients admitted
options.C: Arranging staff and resources for safe patient care
options.D: Lowering the monthly salary costs for the hospital

explanation: Great job! Unit organization is all about setting up people and materials so that care flows smoothly and safely. Keep it up! [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h1)

question: What usually happens in a ward that is poorly organized?

options.A: Doctors take over all daily medication administration tasks
options.B: Patient recovery times become much shorter automatically
options.C: Staff experience chaos and higher risks of clinical errors
options.D: Nurses have more time to spend on personal rest breaks

explanation: Spot on! When things lack structure, confusion creeps in, tasks get missed, and mistakes happen. Good organization keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h1)

question: What does the hospital chain of command mainly show?

options.A: The budget allocated for purchasing medical supplies
options.B: The exact order in which patients are discharged
options.C: The line of authority and reporting relationships
options.D: The schedule for cleaning patient rooms and equipment

explanation: You got it! The chain of command simply tells you who reports to whom and how decisions move up the ladder. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why do modern nursing units often prefer a flat organizational structure?

options.A: It empowers frontline nurses to make quicker decisions
options.B: It removes the need for any nurse managers or supervisors
options.C: It guarantees that every patient has a private room
options.D: It completely stops nurses from ever working night shifts

explanation: Exactly! Cutting out too many layers of management helps nurses act faster and talk directly with leaders when patient needs arise. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h2)

question: When assigning nursing duties on a shift, what should guide you besides just counting patients?

options.A: The specific brand of medication being used
options.B: The personal friendship groups of the staff
options.C: The age of the nurses working that shift

explanation: Well done! Sicker patients need way more time and attention, so illness severity is always the top factor in staffing decisions. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h3)

question: A charge nurse is planning a shift with several very sick patients. What is the safest staffing approach?

options.A: Rotate every nurse to a different room every single hour
options.B: Assign all junior nurses to the most complex patients alone
options.C: Pair experienced nurses with junior staff to ensure safe care
options.D: Keep all senior nurses on one shift and all juniors on another

explanation: You're learning fast! Mixing skill levels protects patients and gives junior nurses fantastic mentorship on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which care delivery system assigns specific tasks, like giving out meds or doing wound dressings, to different nurses?
explanation: Spot on! Functional nursing divides the workload by specific tasks across the whole ward, like a factory assembly line for care. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is the main feature of team nursing?

options.A: A registered nurse leads a group of staff to care for assigned patients
options.B: Patients manage their own care without nursing supervision
options.C: Doctors perform all nursing procedures during morning rounds
options.D: Every nurse on the ward cares for every patient equally

explanation: Correct! In team nursing, an RN guides assistants and junior colleagues to look after a specific group of patients together. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h4)

question: What does the abbreviation SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: You got it! SBAR is your trusty tool for sharing clear, snappy patient updates with doctors and fellow nurses. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why are structured handovers so important on a nursing ward?

options.A: They replace the need for writing patient care plans
options.B: They prevent critical patient details from being missed
options.C: They ensure that nurses never have to work overtime
options.D: They allow doctors to avoid talking to nursing students

explanation: Exactly! Good handovers make sure vital changes in a patient's condition don't slip through the cracks during shift changes. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h5)

question: How should you decide which task to tackle first on a busy morning shift?

options.A: By starting at room one and working sequentially down the hall
options.B: By leaving difficult procedures until the very end of the day
options.C: By addressing life-threatening needs and unstable patients first
options.D: By doing all the paperwork before touching any patients

explanation: Brilliant! Always prioritize the most unstable patients. Safety first, paperwork second! [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h6)

question: You receive your handoff report and hear about four different tasks. Which one needs your immediate action?

options.A: A non-urgent blood pressure check for a stable patient
options.B: A missing signature on a nursing admission form from yesterday
options.C: A patient reporting sudden chest pain and shortness of breath
options.D: A routine discharge education session scheduled for the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Chest pain and trouble breathing point to an emergency that takes priority over any routine paperwork. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT used to measure the quality of a nursing unit?

options.A: Patient fall rates and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: Medication error tracking and incident reports
options.D: The favorite holiday destination of the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Quality care is measured by safety outcomes and patient happiness, not personal staff trivia. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h7)

question: What is the main reason for investigating a medication error on the ward?

options.A: To identify system and workflow issues that caused the mistake
options.B: To reduce the amount of documentation nurses must complete
options.C: To prove to patients that mistakes never happen in the hospital
options.D: To find a single staff member to blame and punish publicly

explanation: Well done! Modern nursing looks at errors as broken processes to fix, rather than just blaming individuals. That's how we build safer hospitals! [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h7)
